pages.text: $(bold)The Fuel Cell$(reset) stores reactor fuel: liquid fuel must be canned before it can be placed in a fuel slot.$(li)Capacity: $(bold)10 L = 10,000 mb$(reset)$(li)Filled by the $(bold)Fuel Canner$(reset); an empty cell can be reused repeatedly$(li)Contents determine performance; the same can behaves differently depending on the fuel (see page 3)$(br2)The complete liquid-to-can line is in $(l:akaishi:liquid_fuel)Liquid Fuel Chain$(/l).

$(bold)Heat Sinks$(reset) provide the reactor's primary cooling; six grades exist: $(bold)Poor → Normal → Good → Fine → Exquisite → Ultimate$(reset), crafted tier by tier.$(li)Heat removal increases from about 1% to 7%; higher grades cool more and last longer$(li)They are fitted into the reactor's cooling components and only operate when touching a fuel rod$(li)Consumable: they wear down while the reactor runs and must be replaced when broken$(br2)Starter recipe: 1 Cooling Base + 4 Copper Ingots = 1 Poor Heat Sink.

$(bold)Fuel determines output:$(reset) the liquid inside the cell sets the energy utilization multiplier: World Base Fuel 3 / Nether Compound Fuel 4 / End Mixture Fuel 4 / Advanced Mixture Fuel 5 / Pure Fuel 8 / End Dragon Fuel 7 / $(bold)Ultimate Mixture Fuel 14$(reset).$(br2)A higher multiplier produces more power from the same cell; the burn rate does not change, only the output.$(br2)Temperature determines safety: $(bold)400-700℃$(reset) gives full output, $(bold)850℃$(reset) is a warning, and $(bold)1000℃$(reset) starts the explosion countdown; details are in $(l:akaishi:reactor)The Reactor$(/l). Higher-tier fuels are covered in the Liquid Fuel Chain and the Plasma Chain.
Reading order: fuel and cooling interaction is described in The Reactor, fuel refining in the Liquid Fuel Chain, and the final tier in the Plasma Chain.
